newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down on importers' activity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down on importers' activity.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar finished lower against its American counterpart on Monday as importers' commercial demand for the U.S. dollar increased, dealers said.
The local unit finished at T$27.753, back from an intra-day low of T$27.769, against Saturday's T$27.727 close. Turnover through dealers was US$207 million.
Dealers attributed the Taiwan dollar's downtrend mainly to importers' greenback demand and some investors' short-covering on the U.S. currency.
Taipei's surprise overnight cutting of ties with the Bahamas had a minor psychological impact in early session, they said.
"Even without the severance of relations with the Bahamas, the Taiwan dollar is in a slow depreciation trend," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Taiwan said late on Sunday it severed diplomatic ties with the Bahamas after learning the Caribbean island was preparing to establish ties with Taiwan's arch rival, communist China.

Analysts say the switch by a country long seen as a staunch ally of the exiled Republic of China on Taiwan could portend similar swings by other Latin American states that are among the 30 countries recognising Taipei rather than Beijing.
Dealers said the U.S. dollar's recent overseas depreciation against the yen had not been a major factor in Taiwan trading, as the Taiwan dollar was taking its cues mainly from local circumstances.
A trading range of T$27.73-78 was seen for Tuesday.
